A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same selective-inference framework and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Renamed packages, reordered datasets, and renumbered figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of error control and power, experiments on eight real-data tasks, and robustness experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulation, real-data, and robustness results, plus computational-time experiments in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: Appendix F.2 adds a condition requiring the imputation matrix selected during the line search to match the observed selection when computing the post-CV p-value. This changes the described inference procedure for adaptive imputation; the pipeline components and underlying DAG-based search remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The real-data evaluation replaces Abalone with Airfoil Self-Noise. The other seven tasks remain, although their Data1–Data8 identifiers change. The larger synthetic datasets and additional pipeline configurations concern experimental settings rather than new task coverage.

E2.justification: Both versions compare against oc and naive for synthetic error control, exclude naive from power comparisons, and compare against oc on real data. Appendix D.1 retains the same comparator definitions.

E3.justification: Listing 3 changes the documented CV setting from five folds to two, without establishing which experiments were rerun. The new runtime study varies sample size from 400 to 1600 and feature count from 40 to 160 across Default, Parallel, and Serial pipelines. Existing main simulation and subsampling settings otherwise remain.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.3 examines runtime sensitivity to sample count, feature count, and pipeline structure. The estimated-variance and non-Gaussian-noise robustness analyses in Appendix E already existed; their relocation and updated plotted values do not constitute new robustness questions.

E5.justification: Listing 3 drops the explicitly specified random_state=0 seed. The reported 10,000 simulated datasets per setting and 1,000 real-data subsamples remain unchanged. No new performance uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: The empirical results are substantially revised: Table 1 replaces Abalone results with Airfoil results and changes values across retained datasets, several simulation and robustness curves change, and runtime findings are added. For example, Concrete at n=200 changes from .74/.09 to .80/.08 for proposed/oc. These are revised results, not a demonstrated same-setting gain, given the changed documented CV configuration.

T1.justification: Section 2 replaces general Gaussian covariance Sigma with independent noise of variance sigma squared, aligning the setup with the existing Theorem 1. Appendix F also revises the conditioning argument to account for response-dependent imputation selection. The three main theorems and their Appendix B proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, and conclusion explicitly frame the work as a proof of concept for feature-selection pipelines in linear models. The contribution list newly asserts the first unified application of SI across multiple analysis components. The central validity and modular-implementation claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies the distinction between using CV to select a pipeline and obtaining valid significance afterward. It adds interpretations of runtime dependence on sample count and pipeline structure. The conclusion removes v1's explicit warning about exponentially costly exhaustive pipeline selection and instead discusses future AutoML integration.

D1.justification: The implementation examples switch from pipelineprocessor to si4automl and document PipelineManager, list-valued parameter choices, and manager composition. v2 also updates the supplementary-material address and adds a demonstration-video reference, dataset citations, DOIs, and licensing information. Hardware specifications remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work coverage is substantially revised. Academic AutoML references are replaced with Microsoft, Amazon, and Google tools; discussion and citations covering several nonlinear and extended SI approaches are removed. Dataset references are added, and the positioning strengthens from limited prior exploration to an explicit first unified multi-component SI claim.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, much of the introduction and related-work discussion, contribution list, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around feature-selection pipelines and two explicit technical challenges. Dataset descriptions move to Appendix D.5, and implementation explanations are revised. The main technical section sequence remains.

P2.justification: v1's separate three-panel error-rate and power figures become one six-panel Figure 3. v2 adds runtime plots and pipeline schematics, redraws existing plots with revised axes and legends, and relocates or resizes Figures 1–2 and Table 1. These changes substantially reorganize the graphical presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves statistical coherence by aligning the noise assumption with Theorem 1 and accounting for adaptive imputation in Appendix F. Clearer scope and new runtime evidence also help assess applicability. The gain is limited by unexplained empirical-value revisions and removal of the explicit exhaustive-search limitation; the core framework and conclusions remain largely intact.
